active_inquiry.handoff_conclusion: Observed in M1: the exact native MuJoCo 3.12.0 runtime uses a 0.002 s timestep and 10-step frame skip (0.020 s control interval), with 0.5 damping, 0.01 armature, and compiled geometry-derived link masses/inertias. The compiled actuators apply +/-5 generalized force for unit actions. Across four in-limit postures and both joint pulse signs, one unit action held for one control interval produced joint speeds up to about 6.1 rad/s and endpoint speeds up to about 0.61 m/s; at several postures the endpoint moved more than 1 cm within the first interval and continued moving during the next intervals. After 0.5 s of zero input, joint and endpoint velocities were near numerical zero, but the endpoint remained at its displaced pose. Interpretation: the leading physical explanation is responsive dynamics with a narrow braking/stabilization margin, not insufficient torque authority or slow passive settling. This supports prioritizing full-hold behavior over reach-only progress. Competing explanation still consequential: a learned policy may nevertheless fail mainly because the baseline training distribution omits inner radii 0.06-0.14 m, or because the stateless observation cannot support hold regulation. M1 cannot distinguish those policy-level causes because no policy was tested, used only four postures and isolated pulses, and did not measure target-directed trajectories or 2 ms continuity during a hold. Therefore the claim is limited to the compiled plant and pulse regime, not to learned-policy success or the official goal.
